title: 54th sitting of the 20th Majlis
summary: The sitting opened with the Speaker announcing the agenda and noting that a Media and Broadcasting Commission bill had been withdrawn. Members then held the preliminary debate on the government's bill to amend the Sports Act (Law 30/2015), sponsored by the Dhidhdhoo member; every speaker backed it, with debate on sports facilities, associations, the proposed sports fund and past governments' records. After a recess the House began debating the 2025 state budget, and the text part ends in the middle of the third budget speech. This part continues the debate on the budget committee's report on the 2025 state budget. Seven members took the floor: some criticised the budget for lacking project detail for their constituencies, for cutting Aasandha and subsidies, and for school and health-centre funding, while others backed it, saying it was well planned and that opposition claims were misleading. The chair ended the day's work at the midday prayer call and again after the break because several members who wanted to speak were in committee work, saying debate would resume at the next sitting on Wednesday 27 November 2024 at 9:00. The text layer is garbled in places and the opening lines belong to a speaker whose header is in part 1.

items.title: 2025 state budget: debate on the budget committee's report
items.outcome: debate continued; adjourned for the day with debate to resume at the next sitting (no vote in this part)

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: Said Maldivian sport has fallen behind regionally and that successive presidents have built grounds.
Said atoll youth centres lack equipment, support is concentrated in Funadhoo, and sport should be kept out of politics.
Hoped for answers by February to the committee's recommendations, and raised cuts to some large schools' budgets.
Asked for separate budgets for schools and health centres, and fairer sharing of development projects across constituencies.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Supported the bill and criticised earlier governments over unfinished sports grounds and idle youth centres in his area and Foddhoo.
Raised a point of order objecting to a remark about the Yameen government; the chair said it was not a valid point of order.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Supported the bill and said sport improves when NGOs and associations are given real power; criticised the state of the football association (FAM).
Said the report did not reflect the floor debate and asked for island-level project lists, citing a formal request letter.
Argued savings could come from embassy and prison costs, and raised unfulfilled commitments for Kurinbi and Vaikaradhoo.

speakers.name: Hussain Hameed
positions: On the bill: backed decentralised tournaments hosted by islands, but doubted a new sports fund can be trusted after the FAM funding case and said commissions have multiplied.
On the budget: supported it, said it rests on the president's pledges, and listed housing loans and local works for his constituency.

speakers.name: Hussain Shareef
positions: On the bill: supported it and tied youth discipline, health and lifestyle disease to sport, suggesting military-style training in schools.
On the budget: discussed revenue of about MVR 34 billion in 2024 and 39 billion estimated for 2025 and the need to manage spending.

speakers.name: Abdul Latheef Mohamed
positions: Introduced the amendment as a way to support all sports and age groups through a decentralised system and urged all members to back it.

speakers.name: Munthazim Ibrahim
positions: Backed the bill but said the Sports Corporation created in 2015 has done no sports work and that associations need stronger budgets and leadership.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Supported the bill, including the national sports framework and commissioner role, and asked for cricket and tennis facilities in Thinadhoo within five years.

speakers.name: Ahmed Naseer
positions: Said youth had few facilities for years; wants first aid and medical services at sports venues, school sports funding and proper grounds.

speakers.name: Hassan Mufeed Abdul Gadir
positions: Supported the amendments, citing inclusion, fair play, and sport as a tool for social cohesion and public health.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Shujau
positions: Supported the bill, praised island councils for running tournaments and welcomed the planned sports fund.

speakers.name: Hussain Imran Latheef
positions: Welcomed the bill, highlighting a national sports institute, legal status for the Paralympic committee and a new anti-doping agency.

speakers.name: Mohamed Shamin Habeeb
positions: Supported the bill but doubted regulations alone help; said Kurendhoo teams get little ministry or association support for tournaments.

speakers.name: Dr. Anara Naeem
positions: Supported the bill, noted Huraa's football record, and said the sports institute and commissioner changes would strengthen sport across islands.

speakers.name: Abdulla Rifau
positions: Supported the bill, saying the Sports Corporation goals set in 2015 were never met, and welcomed the commissioner and sports medicine provisions.

speakers.name: Mohamed Shameez
positions: Supported the 2025 budget, arguing named projects in past budgets were never finished and this one funds projects through to completion.

speakers.name: Ahmed Didi
positions: Said he did not support the budget: the committee report changed nothing and gave no project detail for constituencies or islands.
Questioned the assumed US$500 revenue per tourist as unexplained.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Hussain
positions: Backed the budget, saying it funds housing, health and education and is more detailed than critics claim.
Said the opposition misleads the public, and pointed to the Aasandha spending changes and projects such as Hulhumale' Phase 3.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Said the committee made no changes despite the debate, and worried future budgets could tax inheritance and burial plots.
Said health and education workers' rights and school funding were underfunded, and that nothing was included for Kendhoo.
Raised Islamic University and employment tribunal funding concerns.

speakers.name: Meekail Ahmed Nasym
positions: Said the budget was passed on unchanged and cuts Aasandha while spending on travel and cabinet insurance rises.
Argued recent constitutional changes weaken Parliament's ability to hold the government to account.

speakers.name: Ismail Nizar
positions: Fully backed the budget and report, said the opposition misleads people, and said Aasandha is not cut.
Pointed to the listed PSIP programmes for islands and supported the subsidy changes.

decisions: The Speaker announced the agenda for the sitting.
The Speaker announced that the Media and Broadcasting Commission bill had been withdrawn on 19 November 2024 under rule 101.
The Speaker allotted four hours of debate on the Sports Act amendment bill, split by party (PNC 2h35m, MDP 33m, MDA 14m, Jumhooree 12m, MNP 12m, 7m for each non-party member).
The chair ruled the Velidhoo member's objection was not a point of order.
The House recessed from 10:30 to 11:01 and then began the 2025 budget debate.
The chair paused the sitting for midday prayer from 11:55 to 13:00 and, on resuming, ended the day's work early because members who wished to speak were in committee meetings.
Debate on the 2025 budget report is to continue at the next sitting, Wednesday 27 November 2024 at 9:00.
